items.title: Microsoft Researchers Show AI Agents Can Be Backdoored by Editing Fewer Than 10 Neurons
items.reason: Microsoft's 'Lazarus' shows an AI model can be backdoored by editing <10 rarely-used neurons, no retraining or fine-tuning data needed; concrete repro and a weight-comparison detector with real precision/recall numbers. Exactly the model-supply-chain-compromise angle Mine always-surfaces, with a working PoC.
key_facts: Microsoft's 'Lazarus' backdoors a model by editing fewer than 10 rarely-firing neurons, no retraining needed
Nemotron-Terminal-8B: 7 of >12,000 last-layer neurons edited, trigger command appeared in >=98.8% of triggered sessions, 0% of clean sessions
Qwen3.6-27B and Gemma-4-31B-IT: 51-99.5% success depending on setup; Qwen needed only 6 neurons
Terminal-Bench pass rate fell 46.59% -> 42.05% on the backdoored model; AIME math scores mostly preserved
A weight-comparison detector flagged 91.4% of edited checkpoints with 9.7% false positives (small test set: 35 edited/31 clean)
Asking Claude Opus 5.5 or GPT-6 Astra to just inspect checkpoints performed poorly as a detection method
Microsoft credits Claude Code (Opus 4.5) with helping find the core idea; mitigation is weight-level checkpoint diffing vs. base model

items.reason: 35,578 publicly-open Grok-built apps found, ~1 in 10 leaking real internal data (hospital employee lists, ICU briefing, plaintext passwords) from 30+ organizations including 6 Fortune 500s. Concrete numbers, real-world harm, and a textbook AI-vibe-coding security failure — exactly the shadow-IT risk this newsletter tracks.
key_facts: Claroc found 37,571 Grok-built apps; 35,578 open to anyone without login
~1 in 10 open apps contained internal business or personal data; ~2% rated high/critical severity

Root causes: 'Anyone with the link' as the default share setting, guessable/searchable grok.me subdomains via passive DNS, and a broken Grok-generated membership check (new users auto-approved before the check ran)

items.title: We Built An Agent That Broke All of Our Security Rules. Here's What We Learned.
items.reason: A vendor's own postmortem on a browser/UI agent (Rehearsal) that broke every one of its stated agent-security rules by default (no separate identity, no scoped access, no distinguishable audit trail) because the session cookie can't tell agent clicks from user clicks. No benchmark numbers, but a concrete, first-party account of an agent-identity failure mode that's still mostly unsolved industry-wide (WebMCP, Web Bot Auth are still drafts).
key_facts: Token's UI agent 'Rehearsal' acts inside the user's authenticated browser session, so the server can't distinguish its actions from the human's
It broke the vendor's own stated rules: agents need their own identity, scoped access, and separate audit trails

Fixes required owning both agent and app: dimming/locking the UI during agent actions, logging every action (including blocked ones), capping agent permissions below the user's own (read-only dashboards, approval-gated saves, off-limits secret fields)

Emerging partial industry fixes cited: Chrome's approval-gated auto-browse, Microsoft's per-site agentic browsing pause before passwords/cards, the WebMCP draft (Google/Microsoft, W3C), and the IETF's Web Bot Auth draft

items.title: What objective is reasoning solving?
items.reason: A genuinely novel conceptual framing of LLM reasoning as pathfinding/success-probability optimization, deriving known RL-training behaviors (why CoT grows longer, why extra thinking plateaus, reward hacking) from one lens. Essay, not a paper, so the bare-arxiv override doesn't apply; reasonable HN traction (149 pts) without being over-saturated.
key_facts: Argues reasoning models optimize success probability over the distribution of sampled chains-of-thought, not correctness of any single path
Shows the REINFORCE policy-gradient update with binary reward is equivalent to rejection-sampling fine-tuning on the model's own successful paths, scaled by success rate
Explains why CoT length grows under RL training (successful paths tend to be longer) and why extra 'thinking' helps then plateaus (trained-in habit, not inherent value)
Frames reward hacking as arising from both an imperfect verifier and a sampler finding shortcut regions, worsening with more RL scale
